November 24, 2026 — Neon beats Astra and Fable on LiveBench and cuts Theo’s TS Rust benchmark runtime by 48.6%.
Three months ago, shortly after the Demis/Dean/etc departures , and with disappointing progress on Gemini 3 models, people had publicly given up on Google DeepMind as a frontier lab. Today, apologies are being issued , and Neon is the talk of the town!
Despite giving Gemini 4 Argon (RIP), Carbon and Neon the title story (with Hydrogen a near miss ), we are exercising yet another rare double-feature choice to highlight the unusually strong breakout trend in Neon’s adoption:
If this seems like a coordinated hype campaign, it very probably isn’t, mostly because the names we feature can’t be bought, especially coming up to the end.
AI News for 11/23/2026-11/24/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews' website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies!
Frontier Models as Research Engines: VP ≠ VNP, Protein Design and 948 Kernel Bugs
VP ≠ VNP, posted by two labs : An Anthropic GitHub repo reportedly contains a proof by an internal Claude research model that VP ≠ VNP. This is the algebraic analogue of P vs NP, posed by Valiant in 1979, and implies that polynomials such as the permanent lack small circuits over every field ( @kimmonismus , repo pointer ).
OpenAI's counter-release : OpenAI then posted its own proof and says it was "obtained on November 6, 2026." Neither lab named a model or published an announcement ( @AndrewCurran_ ).
Scope : The result does not imply P ≠ NP, which still requires general Boolean circuit lower bounds ( @ZhihuFrontier ).
Speculation : Curran argues that both labs are sitting on unreleased results and repeats unconfirmed rumors of cryptography breakthroughs. Treat this as opinion.
Riemann proof clarifications : Levent Alpöge says the "250,000+ pages" claim was a joke. He released only the Lean code because he could not produce a readable writeup, and called it "full of garbage obviously, but compiles" ( @kimmonismus , @simonw ).
Lineage claim : A Zhihu analysis traces Alpöge's key method to a short OpenAI proof excluding Landau–Siegel zeros. This is an attributed inference ( @ZhihuFrontier ).
GPT-6 protein design, wet-lab validated : OpenAI released a preprint showing GPT-6 models designing new protein shapes and sequences through reasoning and code, without specialized bio models ( @OpenAI ).

IT之家 11 月 25 日消息，彭博社昨日（11 月 24 日）发布博文，报道称“人类史上最大 IPO”上市（11 月 19 日）的 Anthropic 首次跌破每股 83 美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 554.3 元人民币） 的 IPO 发行价， 美国东部时间 11 月 24 日 16 点（北京时间 25 日凌晨 4 点）收报 81.91 美元 （现汇率约合 547 元人民币） ，单日下跌 6.54%。
这家上周刚创下纪录登陆纳斯达克的 AI 公司，上市首日曾以 111.50 美元 （现汇率约合 744.6 元人民币） 开盘，较发行价高出 34%，盘中一度突破 115 美元 （现汇率约合 768 元人民币） ，完全稀释估值一度超过 2 万亿美元 （现汇率约合 13.36 万亿元人民币） 。
然而，短短数个交易日后，市场情绪迅速逆转。Anthropic 盘中最低跌至约 76 美元 （现汇率约合 507.5 元人民币） ，较发行价低近 9%，较上市首日高点回撤约 34%；路透社测算，其市值一度面临蒸发近 2,000 亿美元 （现汇率约合 1.34 万亿元人民币） 的压力。
本轮下跌并非 Anthropic 独有。市场对 AI 企业盈利能力、巨额算力资本开支以及高估值可持续性的疑虑升温，引发科技股广泛抛售。上周，标普 500 指数与道琼斯工业指数双双进入技术性回调区间，英伟达则录得 2008 年以来最大单周跌幅。
值得注意的是，尽管英伟达在黄仁勋恢复 CEO 职务后带动 AI 相关股票一度反弹，Anthropic 仍未能跟随上涨，彭博社认为投资者正更严格审视 AI 公司的基本面与现金流。

作为10月6日发布的一部分，我们在矩阵乘法指数上取得了一个特别干净的进展，得到了9/4的新上界。自那以后，模型一直在研究这个指数的下界。这已经相当疯狂了，因为关于下界此前一无所知！今天我们宣布，实际上9/4是紧的……这真的是那种我从没想过这辈子能见到的结果。

As part of the October 6 release we had a particularly clean advance on the matrix multiplication exponent, with a new upper bound of 9/4. Since then, the model has been working on a LOWER BOUND for this exponent. This is already pretty crazy since NOTHING was known for lower bounds! Today we announced that actually 9/4 is tight ... This is really the kind of result that I never thought I would see in my lifetime.
(btw, by an "old" result of Yin Tat Lee and collaborators this also implies that linear programs can be solved in time n^{9/4}.)

I gave a keynote at the AI Engineer Code Summit a couple of weeks ago, constructed around the idea that there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of LLMs and coding agents in the past twelve months.
Here’s the video of the talk. In this post I’m going to pull out the major inflection point theme and interrogate it more deeply.
Today, November 24th 2026, is the one year anniversary of the release of Claude Opus 4.5 . With hindsight, this was a consequential model.
In the Opus 4.5 announcement, Anthropic said:
Testers noted that Claude Opus 4.5 handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding. They told us that, when pointed at a complex, multi-system bug, Opus 4.5 figures out the fix. They said that tasks that were near-impossible for Sonnet 4.5 just a few weeks ago are now within reach.
Claude Code was 9 months old at that point, having been introduced alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet on February 24th, 2025.
Opus 4.5 was the first model I had used with Claude Code where the default result was generally the right thing. I hadn’t been using Claude Code as a daily driver because it didn’t feel reliable enough—I had to correct it often enough that it didn’t feel like a clear accelerant.
The new Opus changed that. For most of the coding problems I faced on a daily basis, Opus would get them right . It was clearly faster than working through the problems myself.
Also in November, OpenAI released GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, GPT-5.1-Codex, and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max. These had a similar effect on their Codex coding agent: it became reliably useful for many of my coding tasks.
The timing was convenient, because the December holidays were upon us. A lot of people, myself included, spent December tinkering with these new tools to see what they could do. By January we were ready to use them for our actual work.
We got our first hint of Claude Fable in April, when Anthropic announced Claude Mythos and said that it was too dangerous to release , due to its improved cybersecurity capabilities. Mythos was a model that could not just find security vulnerabilities, it could also figure out how to exploit them.
In June we got to see how good that model was for ourselves, with the release of Claude Fable 5—a defanged Mythos, that would solve most problems but would actively block you from using it for security work.

items.excerpt:
Cybercriminals posing as drivers and dispatchers respond to carriers' job postings on social media, Verisk CargoNet says.
As freight theft rates continue to rise, the supply chain risk analysis firm Verisk CargoNet is recommending that shippers, brokers, and carriers tighten their security and verification processes from Tuesday, Nov. 24, through Monday, Nov. 30.
The firm is highlighting a growing scheme in which cybercriminals posing as drivers and dispatchers respond to carriers' job postings on social media, gain access to company email and phone systems, and use those systems to bid on and steal shipments in the carrier's name.
Verisk CargoNet said its concern in 2026 is not only what is being stolen, but how criminals are gaining access to freight. Cybercriminals are operating under the identities of legitimate carriers, and a growing number are able to execute thefts through standard carrier practices.
Among the schemes of greatest concern to Verisk CargoNet this season are highly technical tactics in which criminals operate under the identity of a legitimate carrier. They compromise a carrier's email account, deceive a carrier already hauling a shipment into delivering it elsewhere, or buy an existing carrier’s credentials.
"The groups behind these schemes are patient, and they plan around the calendar," said Keith Lewis, vice president of operations, Verisk CargoNet. "A carrier's email address and phone number are how brokers know who they are dealing with. Guard access to them the way you guard the keys to your trucks."
The firm also flagged certain patterns about holiday cargo theft:
More specifically, cargo thieves in 2026 continue to favor full-truckload shipments of metals and the enterprise computing hardware used in data centers. Targeted hardware includes fully assembled racks and computing platforms, and networking and security appliances. Thieves also target components such as fiber optic transceivers, central processors, graphics processors and memory chips.
The industry’s best defense is to share news of attacks as they occur, the report said. "No single shipper, broker, or carrier can see the whole picture, and the criminals count on that,” Lewis said. “When one company spots a suspicious load, a fake dispatcher, or a cloned carrier and reports it quickly, everyone else can benefit from it."

items.excerpt:
As hyperscalers buy large volumes of servers, racks, components, and spare parts, they need additional material handling equipment and warehouse automation, Interact Analysis says.
Rapid growth in data center construction is creating demand for material handling equipment and warehouse automation to manage the rising volumes of technology components like servers, racks, components, and spare parts, according to a report by Interact Analysis.
The rising demand for logistics services occurs because all the technical hardware that powers data center operations must be stored, staged, integrated, and moved.
Of the different types of facilities in the data center ecosystem, that demand is rising fastest at spare parts & staging warehouses, which act as consolidation centers for components sourced from multiple OEMs for both the build out and the replenishment of spare parts, according to the report titled “Data Centers Drive Growth for Material Handling and Robotics.”
Over the longer term, investments in robotics within data centers themselves also hold a lot of potential, although it will likely remain unrealized in the short- to mid-term, given the complexity of the various tasks required.
Interact Analysis described four types of data centers: Hyperscale data centers are very large facilities operated by major cloud and internet companies; colocation facilities provide shared space, power, cooling and connectivity to multiple customers (broadly analogous to a third-party logistics model); enterprise data centers support the requirements of a single organization; and edge data centers are smaller facilities located closer to users and devices to reduce latency.
And finally, some additional logistics demand will also be generated by server integration facilities, which assemble, configure, and test complete server racks before shipping them to data centers, reducing on-site installation time and accelerating deployment and replacement cycles.

GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery . Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries:
With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library . It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians.
Astra found a diary reference reference to a visit by the vicomte de Chabot dated five days before a date mentioned in the sketchbook at a nearby river, and suggested that Chabot's journal of his travels (only available by order from Cleveland State University) might confirm that the sketchbook was his work.
Are historians due for a round of Deep Blue ? Mark thinks it will be mild:
But if the experience of mathematics is any guide, we can also anticipate that sometime next spring or summer we’ll face a sort of crisis of confidence as we struggle to understand how to respond to agentic systems that can do things human historians cannot. To be fair, that crisis will almost certainly be less profound for us than it is for math. The problem in mathematics, of course, is that solving hard math problems was the whole game. Historians, on the other hand, constantly reinterpret the past in light of an evolving present; we don’t chase a single universal truth. We also (in the ideal at least) write books and articles that are closer to works of philosophy and literature than they are to scientific tracts. Humanity is thus something of a requirement for the production of historical literature.

The post When the Store Stops Stocking, the Distribution Network Inherits the Customer appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A retailer can remove a sofa from the store and free up a surprising amount of selling space. It cannot remove the sofa from the supply chain. The product still has to be stored, handled, loaded, delivered, and possibly returned. In fact, when a customer no longer takes possession at the store, the retailer assumes responsibility for a larger portion of the physical transaction.
That is the logistics consequence of showroom retail. The store may become a better place to sell, but the distribution network must become a better place to execute.
Traditional retail replenishment is built around relatively predictable destinations. A distribution center sends cases and pallets to known stores, often on consolidated routes. Merchandise is received, moved to the selling floor, and eventually carried away by the customer. Direct-to-consumer fulfillment is different. Individual orders leave on different days, travel to different addresses, and carry different service commitments. The basic unit of warehouse and transportation work changes.
There is no reason a retailer cannot manage both models. There is every reason not to assume the same network will handle both equally well.
Take a distribution center designed primarily to replenish stores. Its receiving, storage, picking, and shipping operations may be optimized for case quantities and stable store demand. A showroom-led network creates a different workload: each picking, item-level verification, protective packaging, carrier labeling, and order-specific dispatch.
The distinction sounds operational, but it changes the capital plan. Storage configuration, pick paths, sortation, packing stations, labor deployment, and automation choices depend on the order profile. So does the ability to accommodate peak demand. A warehouse that moves a high volume of cases efficiently may be poorly equipped to process thousands of small, variable orders with tight cutoff times.
Walmart’s October 8 announcement of its Stockton, California fulfillment center illustrates the scale of investment associated with customer-order fulfillment. The more than 900,000-square-foot facility uses automation and high-density storage to increase order capacity. Walmart described reducing a traditional 12-step fulfillment process to five steps. Our GPT‑6 family of models can design new protein shapes and the sequence of their chemical building blocks using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate those designs.
An internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many protein design tasks. Researchers could also guide designs by prompting the model on where a protein should attach and what shape it should take.
In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs showed evidence of binding, or attachment, across five targets. Redesigned antibodies also retained binding. Specialized models helped supply sequences and select candidates for testing.
The models’ written reasoning and code suggest they draw on math, physics, chemistry, and biological knowledge to reason about protein shapes and interactions with other molecules.

Incorrectly shaped proteins can also cause disease and dysfunction. Proteins are made from chains of chemical building blocks called amino acids. Intermodal’s biggest commercial opportunity is not the occasional load that moves from highway to rail at a lower price. It is the freight that remains on intermodal because the service can be incorporated into inventory policy, production schedules and customer commitments. That requires a shift in measurement: from quoted linehaul cost and average transit time to dependable door-to-door performance and the economic cost of variation.
A rail linehaul is one part of an intermodal movement. The shipment begins with drayage, a terminal gate, and a train schedule; it ends with a second terminal, another truck, and a receiving appointment. Every transfer adds a chance of delay. Reliability is therefore not captured fully by train performance or a quoted transit time. A shipment can travel efficiently between terminals and still miss a customer deadline because chassis availability or appointment windows fail at the destination. Averages can also obscure variation: ten shipments arriving near plan may not offset one critical load that arrives after a production cutoff.
The opportunity is substantial. The Association of American Railroads reported that U.S. railroads averaged more than 298,000 intermodal units per week in October 2026, a monthly record for the weekly average. Volume strength demonstrates shipper interest in the mode, but aggregate demand is not a scorecard for every lane or shipment. A network operating near capacity may perform very differently at the origin terminal, on the mainline and in the destination drayage market. Shippers need to evaluate those segments separately before expanding commitments.
What matters most is the tail of the transit-time distribution. A lane that usually arrives in five days but occasionally requires nine can impose more inventory cost than one that reliably arrives in six. Replenishment orders, promotion calendars and manufacturing material requirements are sensitive to the late shipment, not to the average shipment. That is why planners should compare performance at the 90th or 95th percentile alongside median transit time, missed appointments, container availability and recovery after a missed connection.

items.title: Amazon 报告黑客用开源框架 Cairn 驱动 AI 智能体在约 11 分钟内自主发现并利用 0-day
items.description: Amazon 威胁情报报告称，黑客在开源 AI 渗透测试框架 Cairn 上运行的 AI 智能体，仅凭一句「获取 shell 权限」的指令，就自主发现并利用了一个开源医学影像 AI 应用中未修补的路径遍历 0-day，从映射 API 到任意写文件仅用约 11 分钟，随后写入 Python 反向 shell payload 并以 root 权限获得控制。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ygbhvp086wl672gfxuhfgl23x
items.excerpt:
Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
Amazon 威胁情报报告称，黑客在开源 AI 渗透测试框架 Cairn 上运行的 AI 智能体，仅凭一句「获取 shell 权限」的指令，就自主发现并利用了一个开源医学影像 AI 应用中未修补的路径遍历 0-day，从映射 API 到任意写文件仅用约 11 分钟，随后写入 Python 反向 shell payload 并以 root 权限获得控制。
Amazon 的研究给出了 AI 智能体自主发现并利用 0-day 的完整时间线和攻击细节，读者可以据此评估防御响应窗口的变化。
亚马逊表示，AI 智能体最近发现并利用了一个零日漏洞，整个过程除了“获取 root 访问权限”这一条简单指令外，没有任何人工监督。事发目标是一台东亚大学的服务器。
这些智能体运行在 Cairn 上，这是一个开源的 AI 渗透测试框架。黑客用简体中文编写提示词，并把模型配置为中国标准时区，然后给智能体一份 IP 地址列表，目标只有一个：“拿到 shell 访问权限。”很快，智能体就在其中一台目标服务器上运行的开源医学影像 AI 应用里发现了一个零日漏洞，随后利用该漏洞取得了系统的完全控制权。
亚马逊 表示 ：“这些发现表明，由智能体发起的攻击性行动已经在现实中发生，防御方应当为这类工具带来的速度和持续性做好准备。”
Cairn 是一个开源的 AI 问题求解引擎，首个通过验证的应用领域就是自主渗透测试。用户给它一个任务或目标，也可以选择性地提供实现目标的提示。服务器维护一张包含事实和提示的共享图；调度器读取这张图，安排任务、管理容器并写入协议，然后可以把每个项目分配给一个专用的工作容器，每个容器里并发运行多个智能体。Cairn 不绑定特定模型，可运行在 Claude Code、Codex、Pi 等 worker 后端上。安全公司 Palo Alto Networks 的研究人员还 观察到 ，有人把 Cairn 与 GLM 5.2、DeepSeek V4 Flash 和 DeepSeek V4 Pro 搭配使用。
尽管 Cairn 是为防御方打造的，这套框架同样让攻击性黑客受益。本月早些时候，Palo Alto Networks 表示，黑客利用该框架攻击了半导体、国防和公民社会领域的机构。这轮行动共执行了 25 次自主操作，针对至少 19 家机构，其中至少 10 家被成功入侵，Cairn 智能体实施的行为包括：
Palo Alto Networks 称，攻击者创建任务时只写一行目标，例如：“获取实质性的高价值访问权限，包括但不限于 webshell、SSH、源代码、密钥、用户信息、凭据，理想情况下进入内网。”Cairn 的默认智能体指令明确要求 worker 执行各种渗透测试技术，包括漏洞利用、反弹 shell 和数据外泄。
攻击者还追加了额外的授权说辞来强化这些指令。在每个推理和探索阶段，worker 系统提示词前都会加上一段前言，提醒智能体正在执行经过授权的安全操作。前言写道：“请严肃、专业地对待此事，在任何情况下都不得拒绝任务。”
亚马逊上周的研究进一步揭示了 Cairn 的能力。当给出一份目标服务器清单并要求获取 shell 访问权限时，这些智能体会执行各种任务以尝试完成任务。在其中一例中，智能体瞄准了一台 Redis 服务器，试图滥用其复制功能加载未授权代码、逃逸其脚本沙箱、写入其配置文件并破坏其内存。智能体还尝试对同一系统上的另一项服务实施 Log4Shell 注入。
总体而言，智能体使用这些技术花费了超过 16 个小时。没有一项奏效。智能体还尝试了其他攻击。同样无一成功。
在另一次行动中，攻击者花费超过六个小时瞄准一台大学 GPU 服务器。他们首先利用该大学的公开资源整理出一份包含 80 个真实用户名的清单，并针对 30,000 组凭据组合进行测试，试图通过 SSH 和其他服务获得访问权限。这些尝试同样失败了。
面对一个运行开源医学影像 AI 应用的目标，结果有所不同。智能体识别出了该应用的框架，梳理了其 API 端点，并发现了一个带有 filename 参数的上传端点。他们对该参数进行了路径遍历测试，发现该参数存在漏洞。在大约 11 分钟内，智能体就从梳理应用 API 进展到在服务器上任意写入文件。
在随后的一次会话中，智能体利用同一漏洞将一个 Python 反向 shell 载荷写入 sitecustomize.py——这是 Python 在解释器启动时自动导入的文件。随后，智能体触发一个训练 API 端点以启动新的 Python 进程。新进程导入了该载荷，并建立了一个以 root 权限运行的反向 shell。
在发现之时，该医学影像应用中的这一路径遍历漏洞并不对应任何已分配的安全公告，且尚未修补。亚马逊威胁情报部门基于受影响开源项目中不存在任何相应修复、问题、公告或此前在漏洞数据库中的提及，以高置信度评估这是一个零日漏洞。
在后来的一次会话中，攻击者在智能体识别出该零日漏洞后进入循环，并向智能体提供了一个可隧道进入第二个大学网络的代理。
“代理所连接的服务器运行着相同的易受攻击软件，我们推断该行为者曾利用该零日漏洞攻陷该服务器并建立隧道，”亚马逊表示。“该行为者指示智能体利用该隧道瞄准该网络中的其他机器。”
正如亚马逊所指出的，Cairn 及其他 AI 辅助黑客框架的速度和持续性给防御者带来了新的挑战。
“这些案例中的行动节奏压缩了可用于防御响应的时间窗口，”亚马逊表示。“一个能在数分钟内发现并利用零日漏洞的智能体，其完成活动的速度快于许多安全运营中心手动分诊警报的速度。”
Amazon 的研究给出了 AI 智能体自主发现并利用 0-day 的完整时间线和攻击细节，读者可以据此评估防御响应窗口的变化。

items.title: Searching for distant planets with Astra
items.description: See how two amateur astronomers used Codex and Astra to find potential exoplanets in public data from NASA’s Kepler and TESS space telescopes.
items.excerpt:
Two amateur astronomers used Codex and Astra to look for signs of planets in public telescope data. Now they’ve given professional astronomers a few places to look more closely.
Astronomers have confirmed more than 6,400 planets beyond our solar system ⁠ (opens in a new window) since the first ones were announced in 1992 ⁠ (opens in a new window) . A worldwide community of amateur astronomers has long been part of that search. Some comb through public telescope data for small, repeated dips in a star’s brightness that could signal an orbiting planet. Others use their own telescopes to watch for the next dip and share what they see with researchers.
*Data from the NASA Exoplanet Archive’s Planetary Systems Composite Parameters table ⁠ (opens in a new window) . 2026 data are year to date through November 24, 2026.
Astronomers have used AI in this search for years. In 2017, researchers trained a neural network on 15,000 signals from NASA’s Kepler Space Telescope ⁠ (opens in a new window) that astronomers had already examined. From those examples, the model learned to recognize which patterns in starlight were most likely to come from a planet. When the researchers used it to examine weaker signals, one led them to an eighth planet orbiting a star called Kepler-90 ⁠ (opens in a new window) .
Now, tools like Astra are helping amateur astronomers design and run searches of their own, often on data that has already yielded the more obvious exoplanet signals. Kevin Bond, an engineer at OpenAI, came to astronomy through his love of photographing the night sky. He used Codex to search observations of about 100,000 stars from the Kepler telescope, a planet-hunting mission that ran from 2009 to 2018. Ethan Byrd, founder of the email infrastructure start-up Primitive, has always loved astronomy. Working independently of Bond, he tried several AI models before choosing Astra to help him analyze telescope data from about 19 million stars.
Both searches identified potential exoplanets. Bond and Byrd have now turned to astronomers for an independent assessment of their results. Bond contacted an astronomer at the SETI Institute, who ran an independent search and found two of the same signals in the Kepler data. Byrd sent one of his strongest candidates to researchers working on NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. It’s in line for further analysis, and two more candidates are awaiting submission.

items.excerpt:
Maintenance work often breaks down before a technician reaches an asset, especially when requests arrive through disconnected channels.
Calls, emails, and paper notes obscure priorities, ownership, deadlines, and the details needed for a repair. Those gaps create repeat visits, delayed production, uncertain labor costs, and incomplete records for future decisions.
A structured work order process gives each task an owner, a deadline, and a documented result. Maintenance managers comparing work order software should check whether the system can create, assign, complete, track, and report work in one place. The following sections trace how software controls that process through each maintenance stage across the facility.
An organized system begins by converting an observed issue into a record that technicians can act on. The system should also connect each request to the correct asset, procedure, and priority.
Request forms should require a location, asset identifier, problem description, and requester contact information for each submission. Photos and required fields give technicians enough context before they travel to the job.
Once logged, each request needs a consistent priority rule based on safety exposure and operational impact. Current asset condition and the production schedule also determine the appropriate due date for each request. An obstructed emergency route needs immediate dispatch, while a routine adjustment can wait for planned work.
Rules should route work to a supervisor when a request exceeds a preset cost, risk, or skill threshold. Supervisors then approve, reject, or revise the request before it enters a technician’s queue for scheduling.
Planning turns a request into instructions that a technician can complete without a separate search for information. The work order should identify the asset, describe the fault, and set out a clear task sequence. Linked documents give access to manuals, photos, safety steps, and prior repair notes at the point of work.
Assignment requires more than selecting an available name for a shift or location each day. Managers should match a work order’s required skill, shift, location, and estimated duration to a technician.

items.excerpt:
MassRobotics is developing a new marine robotics facility at Boston Fish Pier, providing startups with direct access to Boston Harbor for testing underwater robots, autonomous vessels and other marine technologies.
The facility is being developed in partnership with Massport as part of its Blue Edge initiative, which supports the region’s growing marine technology sector.
Construction is under way, with the facility scheduled to open in early 2028. Industry programming, including demonstrations, workshops and networking events, will begin during 2027.
Located approximately 10 minutes’ walk from MassRobotics’ headquarters at 12 Channel Street, the new facility will allow companies to design and manufacture prototypes at the organization’s existing workshops before testing them in the harbor.
Planned equipment includes a water tank, a floating testing platform alongside the pier, and lifting equipment for launching and recovering marine robots.
Tom Ryden, executive director of MassRobotics, says: “Boston has always been a harbor city, and some of today’s most exciting robotics work is happening in and under the water. Marine startups tell us that finding a place to test is one of their biggest hurdles.
“With the Fish Pier steps from our headquarters, founders can build in our shop in the morning and test in the harbor by afternoon. We’re grateful to Massport for this partnership and excited to help make Boston a global center for marine robotics.”
MassRobotics currently supports more than 100 resident startups, including CRABI Robotics, which develops underwater robots for cleaning ship hulls.
Levi Gershon, CEO of CRABI Robotics, says: “For ocean startups, getting to the water is one of the hardest parts. A facility on the harbor, steps from where you build, will help the next marine company move a lot faster than we could.”
The new facility will also support Boston’s Marine Tech Hub initiative, connecting robotics developers with maritime companies, researchers and investors.
MassRobotics is inviting marine robotics startups and potential industry partners to express interest in the facility ahead of its opening.

Viabot , a Silicon Valley-based robotics company, is expanding its autonomous outdoor property maintenance operations, with its Viabot One platform now servicing 25 million square feet of commercial property across the United States.
The Santa Clara, California-based company develops autonomous mobile robots designed to clean large outdoor areas, including shopping centers, commercial properties, university campuses and other facilities.
Its customers include Fortune 500 retailers, real estate owners, property management companies and utility providers.
Unlike humanoid robots designed to perform a variety of human-like tasks, the Viabot One is a purpose-built, three-wheeled mobile platform specializing in outdoor sweeping, debris collection and supplementary property monitoring.
The robot can collect debris measuring up to 10 inches and is intended for large properties where conventional cleaning operations require significant labor.
Viabot One combines cameras, lidar, depth sensors, differential GPS and dynamic path planning to navigate outdoor environments.
The system is designed to operate around obstacles commonly found in commercial properties, including parked vehicles, shopping carts and pedestrians.
Its capabilities include autonomous tool swapping, battery replacement, route planning and docking. After completing scheduled cleaning operations, the robot returns to its docking station and empties collected debris into standard trash bins.
According to Viabot, its automated battery-swapping system supports operating periods of 12 to 24 hours.
The platform also provides what the company describes as “soft security” capabilities, including loitering detection and asset monitoring.
Viabot says its robotic intelligence has been trained using more than 5 billion square feet of real-world multimodal data.
The company currently operates across eight states: California, Florida, Indiana, Missouri, Nevada, North Carolina, Texas and Virginia.
In September, Viabot announced a $24 million Series A funding round led by Walden International, bringing its total funding to $43 million.
The investment is intended to support engineering recruitment, product development and expansion of its robotics-as-a-service business.

items.description: Mantic 与 Thinking Machines 在 Tinker 上对 Inkling 2 Small 做后训练，得到一个端到端完成研究与预测的预测智能体，其准确度接近 Fable 5.2 (medium)，单次预测成本降低 15 倍。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/yh9lmlhqwoc77d1ii1mvr5d6x

Training a Scalable Forecasting Agent (Guest Post with Mantic)
Mantic 与 Thinking Machines 在 Tinker 上对 Inkling 2 Small 做后训练，得到一个端到端完成研究与预测的预测智能体，其准确度接近 Fable 5.2 (medium)，单次预测成本降低 15 倍。
原文完整给出数据生成、点时工具和奖励设计三层方案，读者可以据此了解端到端训练预测智能体的可迁移做法。
在各大预测市场上，全球范围内有意思的议题大约有 1000 个，但真正可能有用的预测对象，数量要大上好几个数量级。 这一数量级估算剔除了体育、加密货币和提及类市场（参见 Polymarket 的研究）。 作为演示，图 1 展示了在 50 种不同的地缘政治与经济情景下，对 S&P 500 做出的 10 万条预测。
这些预测来自我们用 Tinker 对 Inkling 2 Small 做后训练得到的智能体。它的准确度大致与 Fable 5.2（medium）相当，但每条预测的成本只有后者的 1/15（图 2）。
这次运行需要我们在后训练技术栈的多个环节做出改进，以应对数据稀缺、时点研究的吞吐与延迟，以及奖励信号噪声大的问题。我们把这套技术栈搭在 Tinker 上，原因有三：(a) 它能轻松扩展到数千个并发 rollout；(b) 采用 StableReinforce 的异步强化学习让实验运行时间缩短到 1/3；(c) 成本效益高。
Mantic 的愿景是：大规模 AI 预测，加上这些系统令人瞩目的准确度，将开启全新的预测应用。 2026 年夏天，两个 AI 系统（包括 Mantic）在一项重要赛事 Metaculus Cup 中 首次 击败了全部 600 多名人类预测者。
预测分为两个阶段：研究与预测。在 上一篇文章 中，我们介绍了如何训练模型，在其他智能体完成研究的基础上做出预测。本文则对 Inkling 2 Small 做后训练，让它在单次智能体 rollout 中同时完成这两步。每个环境都会给智能体一道预测题，以及用于时点研究、执行代码和提交概率分布的工具。
要开展这项工作，我们需要：(1) 比公开平台所能提供的更多高质量题目；(2) 快到足以支撑数千个并发 rollout 的研究工具。
我们从热门预测市场入手，但在跨平台去重、并过滤掉偏题和无关紧要的题目之后，能用于训练的只剩很小一部分。
为了解决数据不足的问题，我们构建了一套系统，用 LLM 直接从新闻中生成合成预测问题，思路类似于 Bosse et al. (2026) 和 Turtel et al. (2026) 。我们借助这套系统生成了 45,000 道问题，组成训练题库。我们重点关注定量问题，例如“截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日，日本外务省最近一次报告显示波斯湾还剩多少艘船只？”这些生成的问题与真实分布足够接近，因此模型的表现能够泛化到预测网站上的留出问题（图 4）。
智能体的研究工具返回的是 时点 数据，也就是在提问当时可以获取、而非之后才出现的信息（例如新闻、维基百科、经济时间序列）。
训练期间，我们在数千个并发环境中生成 rollout。在这种规模下，直接调用第三方数据 API 会让训练慢到无法进行。受各接口速率限制的影响，本文描述的这次训练如果按那种方式跑，大约需要九年才能完成。
于是我们改为持续从这些 API 摄取数据，存入自建数据库，以低延迟访问（图 5）。例如，我们 维护 了一份维基百科完整修订历史的专用时点副本：1.32 TB 的索引和嵌入文本。公开的维基百科 API 只能搜索今天的维基百科，而且获取历史版本时每次请求只能返回一个页面；我们的智能体则可以对任意历史日期的维基百科做语义搜索，并在一次查询中读取整批历史页面。
在对现实世界事件做概率预测时，奖励是随机的。就任何单道问题而言，一个过度自信的预测可能胜过一个符合真实潜在分布的预测（示例见图 6）。

Coventry University is leading pioneering research exploring how recycled steel and aluminium could be used in next generation aerospace, automotive and construction applications.
As world leaders bring COP31 – the most prestigious global summit for action on climate change – to an end, researchers at Coventry University’s Research Centre for Manufacturing and Materials are helping create a more sustainable future.
Future propulsion and modern construction method technologies will rely on low carbon materials and advanced engineering should deliver those while also supporting onshoring and strengthening of UK manufacturing supply chains.
The university’s portfolio of projects in this sector – which total more than £6m of investment from UK government and industrial partners – generate a systems approach to understanding how we can extract and utilise materials from end-of-life sources in more efficient ways.
The project utilises advanced sortation methods, digital twins and complex process and optimization models with a four-year plan of work to deliver a step change in how scrap is produced and used.
Stephen Spooner, Professor of Sustainable Manufacturing at Coventry University, said: “Our portfolio of projects look at how we can unlock even greater value from recycled materials and end-of-life goods, opening up new opportunities for their use in manufacturing.
“What we’re trying to do is characterise the material and products to reduce the risk and uncertainty of their use, so companies are more confident in using them.
“We’re also trying to capture a more complete picture of what’s in the material, components and complex portfolio of products we see reaching end-of-life, so we can use them in their most valuable applications both environmentally and economically.”
While recycled materials are already widely used in manufacturing, developing a greater understanding of their composition could help expand their use in applications with increasingly demanding material specifications.

The SDK Beta represents the first practical milestone in Yarbo’s Open Platform strategy, announced in April 2026 during the company’s M Series Kickstarter campaign.
The strategy aims to extend Yarbo’s modular approach beyond interchangeable hardware attachments, allowing users to customize how its robots interact with other software, devices and services.
Yarbo’s robotic platform uses a common mobile base that can perform different outdoor maintenance tasks through interchangeable modules.
With the new SDK, developers will be able to create applications and plugins that connect authorized Yarbo devices with external systems, including smart home platforms, commercial maintenance software and research tools.
Potential applications include integrating mowing information with smart irrigation systems, coordinating snow removal schedules and creating customized voice interactions.
Commercial operators and equipment dealers could also develop integrations for monitoring maintenance requirements, managing service requests and coordinating robotic operations across larger properties.
Yarbo says universities and research institutions could use the platform to investigate outdoor robotic navigation and autonomous operation, drawing on technologies including real-time kinematic positioning, inertial measurement units, stereo vision and odometry.

items.description: KMPG survey found 64% of respondents said technology and AI disruption will have the greatest impact on the their company.
items.excerpt:
The question supply chain managers are asking has changed from ‘How do we prevent bad events?’ to 'How do we see, absorb, respond and adapt when external shocks are unavoidable?’ This is according to a recent report , from KPMG.
The primary reason for asking this new question is that risk is becoming more complex and interconnected, as exemplified by 70% of the respondents to the survey saying their organization’s risk exposure has increased over the past 2 years.
And 56% said that external disruptions involving factors such as energy, cyber, trade or climate will cause severe operational disruption or have a significant impact on their organization’s costs and performance over the next 3-5 years.
When asked which risks were most likely to have the greatest impact on their organization over the next two years, 64% say technology and AI disruption, while 58% say geopolitical conflict and 48% say macroeconomic uncertainty.

Resilience has become a strategic priority, with 28% of respondents feeling that energy security and resilience have become a significant strategic priority for their organization’s senior leadership. items.title: [AINews] Jensen Is Back! and OpenAI Shows Its Pretraining Curve, joined by Microsoft
items.description: November 23, 2026 — Nvidia reinstates its founder, and OpenAI publishes its internal loss curve and proposes a shared training limit.
items.excerpt:
November 23, 2026 — Nvidia reinstates its founder, and OpenAI publishes its internal loss curve and proposes a shared training limit.
Congrats to Sierra on tripling last year’s $10B valuation , and to Z.ai for releasing GLM 5.4 , their first looped transformer following Thinking Machine’s much smaller Inkling Mini 2 from last week. However all these are outshone by today’s twin title stories…
Jensen Huang is back . Eleven days after announcing his resignation , Nvidia announced his return as CEO, president and member of the Board of Directors.
The board voted unanimously after more meetings with Jensen on Sunday and said it received input from senior U.S. officials (aka the Treasury Secretary and the President dialing into the board meeting ). Colette Kress remains CFO, the independent directors’ investigation continues, and Jensen’s Senate hearing is still due in 8 days. Nvidia also formed a board committee for national security and export control.
As Matt Levine points out , with the firing AND the rehiring by this board with involvement from the government, the investigators are now being put in a position of having had the outcome somewhat predetermined for them, because both have demonstrated that they did not need to wait for any further evidence to come to light.
OpenAI put its pretraining loss curve on the record. In Perplexity and Intelligence , Chief scientist Jakub Pachocki plotted base-model log-perplexity back to GPT-3.5 (on their internal held-out coding dataset … which has notable caveats ):
Think of it as how surprised the model is by the next token on a held-out dataset. Lower is better. GPT-3.5 was around 0.99 and GPT-4 around 0.91. When OpenAI put a model around 0.76 (GPT6 Astra) to work on open math problems, hundreds of frontier math problems started falling quickly . Pachocki extrapolates that another jump in capabilities could come around 0.68–0.70.
This is all in context of pacing the frontier . Pachocki proposes that labs agree on a first limit to development and spell out what would let them cross it, such as a successor to chain-of-thought monitoring. Microsoft’s Mustafa Suleyman gave the first win by cosigning and joining in, running MAI-2 Base on OpenAI’s evaluation set and reporting 0.819. We’d need at least a couple more top labs to join this effort for it to gather steam as a real self-regulatory limit, most notably of course, Anthropic.

items.description: Marina Petrova’s dot Aria helps research websites and build proposals, while proactively flagging messages and resolving issues.

How a small business founder’s dot helps her with research and proposals, while alerting her to critical messages and resolving issues.
Marina Petrova is CEO and cofounder of Intentful ⁠ (opens in a new window) , a lean team that helps brands make their marketing interactive, with products such as ads that answer customers’ questions in real time and tools that make website information readable by AI. The company also advises and trains marketers on using AI.
In travel and tourism, Intentful works with destination organizations and local businesses such as hotels, restaurants, and attractions. A custom proposal is part of how Marina wins their business, showing prospects what’s possible and what it would take to deliver.
To keep Intentful growing, she needed more room for that strategic work, but she was spending too much time on research, hunting for files, and formatting decks. Her dot ⁠ changed all that, taking on tasks and meeting Marina’s needs before she even had to ask.

She brought in her dot, which she named Aria, to help her get from research to a proposal she could put her name on in a few hours instead of several days. The Remote Agents Platform turned engineering tasks into API calls: teams delegate the work, execution takes place in a remote sandbox, and the result comes back as a merge request. In the internal security platform, the number of vulnerabilities fixed more than doubled.
iFood maintains more than 15,000 code repositories. Each periodically needs specific tasks performed: validating code to ensure it meets internal standards, fixing vulnerable dependencies, or running an analysis.
None of these tasks is difficult on its own. The challenge comes when those tasks multiply.
“Solving this for one repository is easy. The challenge is solving it at scale,” says Victor Coelho, Senior Software Engineer at iFood. “The Remote Agents Platform is designed to make it possible to solve this at scale across all 15,000 repositories.”
Before the platform, each team tackled the problem in its own way—and they all ran into the same obstacle.
“Before, we had fragmented solutions. Imagine several teams at iFood trying to solve different problems, but without this layer, this agentic runtime, available to them. In the end, those solutions always ran into the same problem.”
What was missing wasn’t intelligence or a use case. It was execution infrastructure. A dedicated runtime .
The team describes the Remote Agents Platform as an API that launches a remote agentic coding task. The cycle has three steps: the user submits a prompt and environment requirements through a REST call; the platform processes the task on a dedicated remote runner inside an isolated sandbox; and the result is retrieved later.
“The platform’s entry point, its interface, is a simple REST API. Users can use this API to create the runs they need. Internally, we handle and manage the entire lifecycle and delegate execution to isolated sandboxes,” he explains. Task progress can be monitored in real time.

Clay ⁠ (opens in a new window) is a self-learning revenue engine designed to help. Using GPT‑6 Astra, GPT‑6 Sol, and other models, Clay enables users to build lists of companies and people, enrich those records using agents, and use that information in go-to-market plays.

从今天起，你可以用 Claude artifacts 创建、运行和分享桌面应用。“安装为应用”功能正在 Claude for Mac 和 Windows 上以 beta 版形式逐步推出。
当 artifact 被安装为 Mac 或 Windows 应用后，它会拥有自己的图标，并在独立窗口中打开，而不是嵌在 Claude 里。你可以把它分享给别人，而且它在与你的电脑交互之前必须先获得你的许可。允许到什么程度由你决定。
每个应用都可以调用 Claude 和你的连接器，并且当底层 artifact 被编辑时，应用会自动更新。这让知识工作者和开发者构建、维护应用的过程都变得更简单。应用向 Claude 发起的请求会计入你所在套餐的使用额度。
Artifacts 最初只是一种用来分享的工作产出，比如图表或网页。现在人们把它当作日常工作的工具，比如一个定期从日历和邮件中拉取信息的会议准备页面，或者一个追踪当天待发货订单的工具。
如果你在工作中依赖某个工具，它就应该像其他应用一样能直接打开，并在有事需要你关注时提醒你。
已安装的应用可以发送通知，也可以把项目添加到菜单栏或系统托盘。你可以为每个应用单独设置权限，Team 和 Enterprise 管理员则可以为整个组织开启或关闭应用权限和完全访问权限。
你的授权只覆盖应用的当前版本，因此每次更新后 Claude 都会重新询问，即使更新是你自己做的编辑也一样。如果应用的某部分来自其他网站，那部分内容可能在 Claude 不再次询问的情况下发生变化。
你只能为你自己制作的应用授予完全访问权限；在 Team 和 Enterprise 中，只能为组织内成员制作的应用授予该权限。Anthropic 不会在你安装前审查应用，所以请只对你信任的应用授予完全访问权限。
向 Claude 描述你的应用，先把它当作 artifact 试用，然后点击“安装为应用”。你无需打包或签名，应用会使用你的 Claude 账号，因此不需要 API 密钥，也不用单独登录。

更新 Claude for Mac 或 Windows，打开一个你每天都会用到的 artifact，然后在分享菜单中选择“安装为应用”。

items.excerpt:
Introducing ShellBench, the benchmark for real-world tasks
OpenClaw 与 Hugging Face 、Red Hat、UC Berkeley 等机构合作推出 ShellBench，基于超过 1000 万条匿名真实智能体交互构建 100 个日常任务，含 90 个 rubric 评分任务（721 项标准，其中 381 项安全标准）和 10 个代码测试任务，共 53,100 次评分运行。
原文给出 ShellBench 的任务设计、12 个模型与 5 个 harness 的结果和成本对比，读者可据此判断模型与 harness 如何影响日常任务完成率。
让 AI 智能体总结一份文档，它大概能做得不错。但让它把几张收据和一张电子表格核对起来，判断哪些信息是最新的，标记出一笔可疑的付款请求，并解释它是怎么得出答案的？可能就没那么好了。
这种贴近现实的测试，要求智能体不仅要找到正确的信息，还要在过程中持续追踪这些信息，而这正是我们推出 ShellBench 想要评估的内容。
ShellBench 是我们与 The OpenClaw Foundation、Parsewave、Hugging Face、Red Hat 和 UC Berkeley 的研究人员合作开发的新基准测试。它基于超过 1000 万条匿名的真实 AI 智能体交互记录，衡量 AI 智能体在人们实际委托给它们的日常工作中的表现。
ShellBench 评估了十二个模型：GPT-6 Astra、Claude Fable 5.2、GPT-6.1 Sol、Gemini 4 Carbon、Muse Wonder Full、Claude Opus 5.5、Muse Wonder 1.0、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Claude Sonnet 5.5、Kimi K3.1 Pro、DeepSeek V4 Pro 和 GPT-6 Luna。这些模型在五种智能体运行框架下接受测试：Claude Code、Codex、Hermes、OpenClaw 和 Pi。
大多数 AI 基准测试都围绕定义明确的问题设计，比如回答一个问题、解一道数学题，或者写出能通过测试的代码。但真实用户为日常工作提出的真实请求，很少这么有条理。更常见的情况是，你让智能体去找一份文档的最新版本、核对来自几十个来源的开支，或者根据一长串邮件往来准备一封回复。
每个测试场景都从一个简短的请求开始（在 90 项按评分标准打分的任务中，请求中位数只有 43 个词），并配有一个贴近现实的工作区（这些任务的工作区中位数是 188 个文件），其中包括邮件、日历导出文件、电子表格、聊天记录、收据、保存的网页和 PDF。
大多数任务都会设置一个复杂因素，比如过时的记录、看起来相似的账户、相互矛盾的信息，甚至可能是恶意的指令。
在这 100 项任务中，90 项按 721 条标准评分（其中包括 381 条安全标准），10 项通过代码测试。对于按评分标准打分的任务，每一条必需的标准都必须通过，任务才算完成。
GPT-6 Astra 以 62.5% 领先，紧随其后的是 Claude Fable 5.2 的 61.9% 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 的 61.4%。前三名之间只相差 1.1 个百分点。
在实际工作中，这意味着如果智能体正在核对付款、确认最新指令或准备一份完整的报告，只要漏掉一项要求，就可能影响这项工作是否可以直接使用。
在 77 项任务中，有 87 条标准用来检查答案是否点明了自己用到的文件，包括那些用于裁定信息冲突的记录。晚餐规划任务就说明了这一点为什么重要。
例如，在一项晚餐规划任务中，531 次尝试里有 522 次选对了餐厅，但有 331 次失败，唯一原因就是推荐结果没有点明支撑该团体预算或时间安排的文件。只有 152 次满足了全部要求。
检索信息、对信息进行推理，以及把信息一直保留到最终答案，是三种不同的能力。智能体可以检索到正确的信息，却仍然没能在最终答案中把它保留下来。
对开发者来说，这意味着提升下一代智能体不能只靠减少幻觉，还要改进智能体追踪需求、保留重要上下文、核验完整性以及说明所用证据的方式。
在 100 项任务的评测中，对五个执行框架取平均，GPT-6 Astra 在三次尝试中至少成功完成一次的任务占 75.1%。
但三次尝试全部成功的比例只有 48.8%。由于每次运行只评判一次，这种波动有一部分可能来自评判方。
值得注意的是，这说明智能体也许有能力完成某项任务，但这并不代表它能持续可靠地完成。只有重复评测才能揭示它是否真的做得到。
ShellBench 还专门关注安全。它的任务纳入了正常工作流程中可能出现的风险，包括钓鱼尝试、欺诈性付款指令、敏感信息和不可逆操作。
在全部 53,100 次运行中，有 15.7% 至少未通过一项安全检查。执行框架的选择对安全性的总体影响很小。即便在满足全部正确性标准的 26,151 次运行中，仍有 2,589 次（9.9%）未通过某项安全要求。
智能体的整体任务完成率并不能取代对完整工作流程的安全审查，这反映出整个智能体生态仍需持续投入的工作。
一个能读取文件、与服务交互并采取行动的智能体，需要判断的不只是某条指令在技术上是否可执行，还要判断这条指令是否恰当、是否获得授权、是否基于可信信息。
在全部五个执行框架中测试过的模型里，同一框架内最高分与最低分模型之间的差距中位数为 45.7 个百分点。
保持模型不变、只更换执行框架，产生的中位差距更小，为 6.2 个百分点。在得分最高的五个模型中，模型选择带来的差距缩小到 15.2 个百分点，执行框架选择带来的差距为 9.9 个百分点。
结果表明，至少就所测试的模型和任务而言，底层模型比它周围的执行框架更能预测任务完成情况。
ShellBench 发现，执行框架会改变智能体的工作方式，包括它们处理多少 token、多久修改一次输出，以及完成任务需要多

items.description: Skills over MCP is in public beta in Claude, so MCP servers can ship skills alongside their tools. Tasks and Elicitation are now generally available, and File Uploads is rolling out soon.

Skills over MCP is now in public beta in Claude, so MCP servers can ship skills alongside their tools. We're also giving servers ways to handle longer, more interactive work with Claude: Tasks and Elicitation are now generally available, and File Uploads is rolling out soon.
Two years ago, Anthropic launched the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a new standard for connecting AI agents to the systems where data lives. The spec has kept evolving to meet the connectivity needs of agents in production, and is becoming foundational for agentic messaging and orchestration.
With today’s updates, Claude can work with a server more like it works with another agent: learning from it, delegating to it, and exchanging input and files along the way.
Tool names and descriptions tell Claude what a server can do, but don't cover how to handle specific use cases. With Skills over MCP , servers can publish skills alongside their tools to help Claude take on longer, multi-step work. Claude loads a skill only when it's needed, keeping context use low. Skills update with the server, so developers can ship tools and guidance together and users have nothing separate to install.
Skills can cover best practices, step-by-step workflows, or even playbooks tailored to a user's account or organization. Using Skills over MCP:
Skills over MCP is in public beta in Claude and Claude Code, on by default for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans and available to Team plans once an admin enables it. Coming soon to Enterprise.

Hand off long-running work with Tasks . Tool calls used to have to finish before Claude could move on. With Tasks, servers can run operations that take time, or even full agent loops, while Claude keeps working and picks up the result when it's ready. GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer . GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this:
In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count.
This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said:
Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality.
GLM 5.4 is not yet available as open weights:
We plan to open-source the model weights responsibly after completing necessary safety hardening.
I tried it out using the Z.ai API, for which I had to sign up for their Coding Plan subscription because 5.4 cannot currently be accessed through the regular API.
It turns out both coding plan and regular API share the same OpenAI-compatible Responses API (at https://api.z.ai/api/v1 ), and the API key for the coding plan worked with that and gave me access to the new model.
I built a llm-glm plugin , then realized that llm-zai by Tommy Hughes already exists! I've shipped mine purely because llm-zai doesn't yet support the new model, but I'll likely retire mine once that plugin catches up.
Here are pelicans for GLM-5.4 on low, high, and max. This is the max one:
I realized I never ran pelicans for GLM-5.3, so here those are for the same effort levels. They look similar in quality to 5.4.
It's interesting how GLM 5.1 and GLM 5.2 produced radically different pelicans from other models. The pelicans for 5.3 and 5.4 are much more comparable to those I get from OpenAI or Anthropic models - the previous generations had their own distinctive look.
I made a comparison grid showing the four generations of GLM pelicans all in one place. The style transition between 5.2 and 5.3 is pretty stark.

The application, US 2026/0364774 A1, was published on November 19, 2026, and was highlighted in a report by Patentlyze, a publication […]
items.excerpt:
Figure AI has filed a patent application for a wearable robotic system designed to capture human arm movements and use the resulting data to train humanoid robots or control them remotely in real time.
The application, US 2026/0364774 A1 , was published on November 19, 2026, and was highlighted in a report by Patentlyze , a publication specializing in patent analysis.
The proposed system consists of a backpack-style frame fitted with two articulated mechanical arms that follow the movements of a human operator.
Rather than requiring workers to perform demonstrations in a motion-capture studio, the equipment could allow movement data to be collected while people carry out everyday tasks in factories, warehouses and other working environments.
According to the patent application, the wearable apparatus includes a harness attached to the operator’s torso, with mechanical arms extending over the shoulders and following the movements of the wearer’s arms.
Each mechanical arm incorporates rigid links, articulated joints and sensors that measure movement at the shoulder, elbow and wrist.
The system can provide up to seven axes of rotation per arm, allowing it to capture complex movements while accommodating different body sizes.
Joint encoders measure rotational positions, while inertial measurement units track orientation and movement. Glove-like attachments connect the ends of the mechanical arms to the operator’s hands.
The design allows the mechanical arms to follow the wearer’s movements without requiring extensive physical attachments along the human arms.
Sensor information can be recorded for subsequent machine learning applications or transmitted to a humanoid robot for remote operation.
One of the more significant features described in the filing is the ability to translate human movement into robot commands with an end-to-end delay of less than 20 milliseconds.
This could allow an operator to control a humanoid robot almost simultaneously with their own movements, potentially improving the responsiveness of remote manipulation.
The patent also describes a clutch mechanism that temporarily interrupts the transmission of movement data.
In one proposed configuration, machine learning software could identify pauses in the operator’s activities and automatically activate the clutch.
A headset could additionally provide the operator with video from the robot’s cameras, allowing the human to observe the robot’s surroundings while controlling its movements.

items.excerpt:
A new autonomous experimental platform enables fully automated experiments on the structural properties of metallic materials.
The system, described in a study published in Science and Technology of Advanced Materials: Methods , offers a basis for closed-loop autonomous optimization of these materials, which will make it easier to develop better structural metals.
Materials science research involves testing a variety of formulations under a range of conditions and measuring many parameters. The number of combinations quickly balloons, and human experimenters can test only a small fraction of those possibilities.
That makes autonomous, automated experiments an attractive approach in materials research, but the systems to carry out such experiments need to be developed.
Platforms have been developed to do autonomous, automated experiments with liquids, powders, and thin films, but working with bulk metallic materials has proven challenging. The new system is designed to meet that precise need.
“Solid metal specimens are difficult to handle automatically, and the experimental equipment often requires considerable space,” explained Yulin Xie of Tohoku University , the study’s lead author. “Our platform addresses this challenge by integrating heat treatment, structural analysis, and mechanical testing into a single automated workflow.”
The team developed a robotic platform that heats solid metal specimens, examines their structure with X-rays, tests their mechanical properties, and then recovers them. The automated handling, treatment, and recovery of each specimen takes about 13 minutes, not including the time for the heat treatment. All manipulation and measurements are performed automatically.
“The platform records how processing affects structure and properties, generating data for AI-based materials development,” said Xie.
The researchers tested the platform with automated experiments measuring the properties of an alloy after one- and two-step tempering. The results were consistent with measurements in manual experiments, validating the automated experimental platform. Xie said the team also demonstrated AI-assisted adjustment of the furnace controls, laying the groundwork for closing the automation loop.
The next step is to enable an AI system to set the platform’s heat-treatment conditions based on the results of the previous experiment. That would create a closed loop where the results of automated experiments guide the design of the next experiment.

items.excerpt:
Motorsport is preparing to enter a new dimension as Airspeeder develops a racing series featuring electric flying cars capable of speeds exceeding 120 km/h, with pilots controlling their aircraft remotely using augmented reality technology.
The company has named Australian navigation technology specialist Advanced Navigation as its official navigation partner, bringing precision positioning and flight control technology to what the organizers describe as the world’s first electric flying car racing series.
The inaugural Airspeeder race is scheduled to take place in Adelaide, Australia, in November 2026, with five pilots representing Australia, the United States, Great Britain, Italy and New Zealand. A second race is planned for April 2027.
Unlike conventional motorsport, competitors will race in three dimensions, navigating virtual racetracks superimposed on real-world environments through augmented reality.
The aircraft themselves will fly above designated racing circuits, with future events potentially taking place over snow, oceans, deserts and canyons.
The Airspeeder Mk3 is an electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft featuring eight rotors, a lightweight carbon-fiber chassis and a 96 kW electric powertrain.
Designed for speeds exceeding 120 km/h, the aircraft can perform sharp turns, rapid acceleration and sudden changes in altitude.
These capabilities introduce considerable technical and safety challenges, particularly when multiple aircraft are racing in close proximity.
Advanced Navigation will equip future Mk3 aircraft with sensors providing real-time information about position, velocity and orientation, allowing flight control systems to respond rapidly to changing conditions.
Chris Shaw, CEO and co-founder of Advanced Navigation, said: “Motorsport has conquered land and sea. The next frontier is the sky. This is one of the most ambitious engineering challenges in modern motorsports, where every gram, every millisecond, and every manoeuvre matters. We’ve spent years developing navigation technology for harsh and demanding environments. Now we’re bringing that expertise to the next evolution of high-performance racing,”
Beyond the racing spectacle, the partnership is intended to provide an experimental environment for technologies that could eventually be used in autonomous aircraft, cargo transportation and other advanced aviation applications.

items.excerpt:
The global robotaxi market is forecast to grow from $486.75 million in 2025 to approximately $179.4 billion by 2034, according to a new report from Polaris Market Research .
The research projects a compound annual growth rate of 92.8 percent between 2026 and 2034, reflecting expectations of rapid expansion in autonomous ride-hailing services as technology advances and commercial operations increase.
Growth is expected to be supported by improvements in artificial intelligence, lidar, radar, cameras and autonomous driving software, alongside investment in electric vehicles and supporting infrastructure.
The report identifies partnerships between autonomous vehicle developers and established ride-hailing companies as an important factor in commercial expansion.
Such arrangements allow technology developers to access existing customer networks and fleet management systems, while ride-hailing operators can introduce autonomous services without developing their own self-driving technology.
According to Polaris, North America accounted for 72.2 percent of global robotaxi market revenue in 2025, supported by investment in autonomous driving technology and early commercial operations.
Asia-Pacific is expected to experience the fastest regional growth, with a projected compound annual growth rate of 93.1 percent during the forecast period.
Electric vehicles represented 69.4 percent of robotaxi market revenue in 2025, reflecting their suitability for autonomous fleet operations.
The research also forecasts particularly strong growth in camera-based sensing technologies, with the camera segment projected to expand at 94.7 percent annually.
Major companies operating in the sector include Waymo, Baidu, Pony AI, WeRide, Zoox, Tesla, Uber and Lyft.
Despite the optimistic projections, the report acknowledges continuing challenges involving safety, regulation, vehicle costs and infrastructure.
The commercial success of robotaxi services will depend on operators demonstrating reliable autonomous driving performance while maintaining competitive fares and managing the costs of fleet operations.

Coprod , which builds hardware components for robotics and physical AI applications, has announced a $6 million pre-seed round to reduce the time and costs associated with building a novel robotic platform.
The round was led by Founderful and Prototype and includes additional investment from General Catalyst, Pace Ventures, Tiny Supercomputer Investment Company, Kima Ventures, SDAC, Unruly Capital and Venturekick, with participation from angel investors Thomas Wolf, founder of Hugging Face, the Dassault Family, Florent Perrichon and other renowned angels.
The compatible hardware components which the company calls “co:products” are already powering multiple robots in the Swiss ecosystem, notably the first student-built Swiss humanoid robot created by the ETH Robotics Club which took its first steps a couple weeks ago in Zurich.
The company is currently establishing new partnerships with other robotics integrators and well known labs to validate the first hardware prototypes before launching them on the market early next year.

With coprod’s stack, the same work only requires a small team of great roboticists, $5,000 to $25,000 per design iteration, and a few months of time.
coprod’s ecosystem of hardware components for physical AI applications, works alongside a seamless software API & front-end configuration tool that interconnects those components and standardises the communication between them while preserving real-time performance required for safe, performant and reliable hardware.
The founders are graduates of the École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) and formed coprod in late 2024 to address the lack of compatibility between robotics components. Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components—HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components—things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird’s even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS .
This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha , which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself!
I’ve been trying it out today, and it’s very impressive. It feels fast, the UI is lightweight and intuitive, and most of the websites I’ve tried to load in it have worked as they should. It looks like this (showing my video-compressor tool):
Here’s the process tree after I opened six tabs in one window and another tab in a second window (generated by this script , thanks Claude):
Ladybird runs different tabs in different processes, an isolation mechanism used by most browsers (well, technically Chrome uses a process-per-site).
I tried Ladybird against several of my more advanced tool examples—like the video-compressor shown above, which runs ffmpeg compiled to WebAssembly. I had it resize its own screenshot using my image-resize tool . It happily runs my Pyodide REPL (Python compiled to WebAssembly) too.
The one thing I tried that didn’t work was Datasette Lite , which runs Pyodide in a complicated arrangement of service workers and web workers. Attempting to start Datasette Lite displays this error:
undefined is not a function (evaluated from 'navigator.serviceWorker.startMessages')
I filed an issue about this , then found a FIXME annotation in the source code.
The project has been leaning heavily into coding agents this year. On February 23, 2026 Andreas Kling published Ladybird adopts Rust, with help from AI , describing how they ported parts of their LibJS JavaScript engine from C++ to 25,000 lines of Rust in two weeks using Claude Code and Codex.
Here’s the GitHub contributions chart for Ladybird over the past twelve months:
That uptick in October corresponds to the landing of a wealth of big improvements.
This Month in Ladybird — October 2026 describes what happened. In addition to moving style and layout to their own thread, landing a new JavaScript JIT, and replacing their C++ with Cranelift WebAssembly engine

Installed more than 2,300 meters above sea level, six Schindler escalators have provided reliable access to Longtoushan’s scenic peaks for seven years, despite extreme weather. As outdoor escalators gain visibility as a smart transportation solution for destinations in China and beyond, the project showcases Schindler’s robust technology and stellar performance in demanding conditions.
Reaching the peak of Longtoushan, or Dragon Head Mountain, in China’s northwestern Shaanxi Province is an unforgettable experience. Perched more than 2,300 meters above sea level, the mountain offers visitors stunning views of forests, unique rock formations and a sea of clouds that frequently surrounds its summit.
Yet these same conditions that make Longtoushan a popular destination, attracting nearly 500,000 visitors each year, have also presented significant accessibility challenges. For much of the year, the steep mountain experiences low temperatures, with heavy snowfall often blanketing the upper elevations during winter and making the journey to the top difficult for many visitors, especially older adults and people with limited mobility.
As scenic destinations across China attract growing numbers of visitors, escalators are emerging as a smart, efficient solution for improving access to mountainous terrain and elevated viewpoints. Recent projects, including the record-breaking Wushan Goddess Escalator in Chongqing, illustrate how vertical transportation solutions can help transform the visitor experience at destinations with challenging topography.
At Longtoushan, six heavy-duty Schindler escalators have provided visitors with convenient access to the mountain’s scenic peaks for the past seven years, withstanding the demanding conditions of this harsh environment.
Installed and maintained by the Swiss manufacturer, the Longtoushan system is one of the longest high-altitude outdoor escalator systems in China and the first high-altitude outdoor scenic escalator installation in the country’s northwest region. Spanning a total length of approximately 170 meters, the six Schindler 9700 escalators help visitors reach the summit while enjoying panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and valleys. Each escalator section provides a vertical rise of 26.5 meters.
“The ‘cloud escalators’ provide accessibility for all visitors,” said Zhiguo Yan, deputy general manager of Longtoushan Scenic Area. “They make it easier for everyone to reach our mountains.”

An open-source runtime that helps operators protect running Linux systems without needing to wait for the patch or restarts
OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect Linux systems while they roll out patches. In a controlled test ⁠ (opens in a new window) , a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without requiring a restart.
We’re inviting developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators across the industry to help develop the project further. The project brings together OpenAI’s frontier AI, security and infrastructure research and Cisco’s infrastructure and security expertise to help protect the systems people rely on every day.
Testing and deploying a patch can still take days or weeks. Protecting a service in the meantime can be challenging because an exploit and a legitimate request may rely on the same Linux operation. Blocking that operation entirely could take the service offline.
Shirudo (Japanese for “shield”) is designed to help security teams navigate this tradeoff. Teams can test whether a temporary safeguard, called a shield, blocks the behavior that exposes a vulnerability while allowing legitimate requests through. Once an operator approves the shield, it can be deployed while the service continues running.
Shirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points inside the operating system. This makes it possible to observe suspicious activity and apply targeted security protections to running systems.

The data center boom is creating a significant new source of warehouse and logistics demand across the U.S., according to a report from real estate firm Cushman & Wakefield.
By the numbers, industrial leasing tied to data center development and operations reached 50 million square feet (msf) through Q3 2026, 113% above the full-year 2025 total and far outpacing the 21% increase in total new industrial leasing nationally, the firm said in its report, “Data Centers: The Newest Logistics Demand Engine.”
Year-to-date U.S. imports of AI-related equipment, parts, and components increased 62% from a year ago to $659 billion, and those goods are moving through ports, warehouses, and distribution networks before reaching data center users.
“Data center development is creating a physical supply chain that extends well beyond the campus itself,” said Jason Price, Head of Americas Logistics & Industrial Research at Cushman & Wakefield. “Servers, power and cooling equipment, construction materials and replacement parts all have to be manufactured, stored and distributed, and that is now showing up as a meaningful new source of industrial leasing.”
Likewise, 3PL leasing tied to data center users reached nearly 11 msf year to date across 10 transactions greater than 500,000 square feet, supported by long-term contracts announced earlier this year between major 3PLs and leading hyperscalers.
That fast growth is adding another source of competition for quality industrial space, since data center-related users—such as hyperscalers, suppliers, and 3PLs—often know where new campuses will be developed before ground is broken and can secure space early.

Five day annual Black Friday-Cyber Monday (BFCM) sales period runs from Thursday, Nov. 26 to Monday, Nov. 30.
The number of shoppers planning to participate in Black Friday-Cyber Monday (BFCM) shopping events this year could hit a 10-year high, but their overall expected spend will remain flat, according to a report from Deloitte.
"We see consumers spend thoughtfully during promotional events throughout the year, and this appears to be holding true for the Black Friday-Cyber Monday shopping period as well, where shoppers continue to be strategic and savvy about their spending,” said Brian McCarthy, Retail Strategy leader, Deloitte.
Most consumers (87%) said they plan to do retail shopping during the annual promotional period, which runs this year from Thursday, Nov. 26—Monday, Nov. 30. But although that percentage marks the highest level since 2016, surveyed consumers expect to spend an average of $624 during the promotional week, which is no higher than 2025.
Sorted by channel, surveyed consumers plan to spend 61% of their budgets online and 39% in store. But about half (47%) of BFCM shoppers also say that rising shipping costs may push them toward stores or pickup.
Participation is expected to be particularly high among Gen Z shoppers (94%), who are planning to spend more than others ($752). However, 40% plan to use buy now pay later (BNPL) options to finance their purchases.
"Whether shoppers use the Black Friday-Cyber Monday period to check a few items off their lists or complete most of their holiday shopping, we anticipate heightened enthusiasm this year. Gen Z shoppers, in particular, appear to be embracing the promotional week as a way to maximize value and stretch their holiday budgets further,” said Natalie Martini, vice chair and US Retail and Consumer Products sector leader, Deloitte.

Deploying robots in real-world settings requires reliable perception throughout an interaction. To pick something up, a robot needs to follow the positions of its gripper and the object as they move. In a laboratory, a robot handling a pipette must keep track of its tip while aligning it with the opening of a tube. These tasks become harder when nearby objects clutter the view, the gripper obscures the object being handled, or the viewing angle changes.
One way to help robots follow these interactions is to track specific locations on the objects they handle. This is the idea behind point tracking . Given a location in one video frame, a tracker estimates where that same point appears in subsequent frames, when it is occluded, and where it reappears. These trajectories can help robots learn from demonstrations, plan and guide movements, and model how objects respond to actions.
Robotics systems often rely on off-the-shelf trackers to automatically annotate motion in videos and provide feedback during execution. And current trackers score well on established robotics benchmarks, suggesting they could be ready for wider use in real-world systems. We wanted to see whether those results hold up across the varied scenes, viewpoints, and object interactions robots encounter in practice.
We introduce RoboTrack , a benchmark and training data suite for point tracking in robotic manipulation. RoboTrack-Bench contains 307 human-annotated videos from DROID, Ego-Exo4D, MolmoAct 2 , and EgoVerse, covering different robots and human hands, cluttered scenes, and first- and third-person viewpoints. To study how training data affects tracking in these settings, we also extend MolmoSpaces , Ai2’s simulation ecosystem for robot learning, to generate dense point tracks from simulated robot manipulation trajectories. This pipeline produces RoboTrack-15M , a new synthetic training dataset targeted toward robotic manipulation.

items.title: Investing in Embo
items.description: a16z leads Embo’s round
items.excerpt:
Robots can already do remarkable things in demos: fold laundry, prepare food, and sort objects. But demos often hide how fragile those skills still are. Move an object, change the lighting, or introduce something unfamiliar, and the robot can struggle.
AI is now moving off the screen and into the physical world, and that requires models that understand how the physical world works. What kind of model will get us there remains an open question. Some teams are building vision-language-action models, while others are extending general-purpose language models to control robots. Embo ’s conviction is that world models are the next generation of frontier AI: models that learn how the world works, enabling robots to anticipate the consequences of their actions, recover from mistakes, and adapt to unfamiliar situations.
For Danijar Hafner, world model agents have been a decade-long pursuit. His doctoral thesis, Embodied Intelligence Through World Models, explored the foundations of this approach. His work on Dreamer showed how an agent can learn to act by practicing inside a learned world model. Most recently, Dreamer 4 learned to obtain diamonds in Minecraft from previously collected data, training its behavior entirely through imagined experience. He’s now bringing that research to Embo, which is building the brain for the humanoid workforce.
To achieve general robot capabilities, the company is tackling two closely related problems: generalization and resilience. A robot trained in one kitchen needs to work in any other kitchen it has never seen before. And when an object slips or a drawer sticks, it needs to recover and keep going. World models allow robots to learn general knowledge and turn that knowledge into reliable skills.
Robotics has traditionally struggled to produce enough general data to train on. Learning from human demonstrations has driven significant progress, but we can’t demonstrate every task in every environment or every way it might go wrong. World models unlock a much larger source: internet video, which contains an enormous record of how objects move, how materials interact, and how people perform tasks. Embo’s approach starts here, training a world model on massive amounts of video and robot demonstrations so that robots learn general knowledge far beyond what could be collected on their hardware.

items.title: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
items.description: Using agent teams and formal verification to improve quantum algorithms for fusion and chemistry.
items.excerpt:
Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg and Ryan Babbush
How using agent teams and formal verification can improve quantum algorithms for modelling fusion energy, chemistry and enzymes
Quantum computers could soon solve problems beyond the reach of classical supercomputers. However, there is a catch: even when using the best quantum algorithms, some important applications still require more resources than early quantum hardware will be able to support.
In a new paper , we used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve well-known quantum algorithms, creating highly efficient quantum circuits. These optimized circuits, which are instructions for how a quantum computer should carry out an algorithm, could one day help us run simulations that solve complex scientific challenges, from fusion energy to drug design. To help the community build on this work, we are open-sourcing our Lean library , problem specifications, and verified solutions on GitHub.
Because we cannot test resource-intensive quantum circuits on classical computers or today's small quantum processors, we have to prove that they work mathematically. Our agent teams proved each result using Lean, a formal theorem prover.
Improving quantum algorithms using agentic teams For each problem, we tasked separate, independent agent teams with finding algorithmic improvements. These ideas were then verified with Lean, before entering a shared notebook. Every four hours, agents from each team met at a virtual conference to trade, debate and compare ideas.
